name: Chicken Chasseur
blurb: Bistro braise of chicken with mushrooms, shallots, white wine, tomato and tarragon.
ingredients: Small bunch tarragon and parsley, chopped
Mashed or boiled potatoes, to serve
method: Season the chicken well. Brown it skin-side down in the butter and oil in a wide pan for 6-7 minutes until deep gold, then turn and colour the other side. Lift out.
Add the shallots and mushrooms to the pan and cook for 6 minutes until browned. Add the garlic and tomato purée and stir for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine, scrape the base and let it reduce by half.
Add the stock and chopped tomatoes, return the chicken skin-side up, and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes until the sauce has thickened and the chicken is tender.
Stir in most of the herbs, check the seasoning, and serve with potatoes, scattered with the rest.

name: Chicken Paprikash
blurb: Hungarian braise heavy with sweet paprika, finished with soured cream, over buttered egg noodles.
ingredients: 8 bone-in chicken thighs or 1 jointed chicken
300g egg noodles or nokedli, cooked and buttered
method: Brown the chicken in the lard in a heavy pan, then set aside.
Cook the onions in the fat over low heat for 12-15 minutes until soft and golden — this sweetness is the base of the dish.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the paprika (it burns easily), then the peppers and tomatoes.
Return the chicken, add the stock, cover and simmer gently for 30 minutes until tender.
Whisk the flour into the soured cream, stir in a ladle of hot sauce to temper it, then stir it all back into the pan and warm through without boiling. Serve over buttered noodles.

name: Tartiflette
blurb: Alpine gratin of potatoes, bacon and onions blanketed in melting Reblochon.
method: Boil the potatoes whole until just tender, cool a little, then peel and slice 1cm thick.
Fry the lardons until crisp, add the onions and cook for 8 minutes until soft. Pour in the wine and let it bubble away.
Rub a baking dish with the cut garlic. Layer in half the potatoes, season, spoon over the bacon-onion mix and half the crème fraîche, then the rest of the potatoes and crème fraîche, with nutmeg.
Cut the Reblochon in half through its middle and lay it rind-side up on top.
Bake at 190C for 25-30 minutes until bubbling and golden. Rest 5 minutes and serve with a sharp green salad.

name: Blanquette de Veau
blurb: A gentle white braise of veal (or chicken) with mushrooms and baby onions in a silky cream sauce.
ingredients: 900g veal shoulder or blade (or use chicken thighs), in large chunks
1 onion studded with 2 cloves, 1 carrot, 1 leek, 1 bay leaf
Chopped parsley and steamed rice, to serve
method: Put the veal in a pot, cover with cold water, bring to the boil and skim off the foam. Add the studded onion, carrot, leek and bay, and simmer very gently for 1 hour 15 until tender. Strain, keeping 700ml of the broth.
Simmer the baby onions and mushrooms in a little of the broth for 10 minutes; set aside.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes without colouring. Whisk in the reserved broth and simmer to a smooth, coating sauce.
Whisk the cream and yolk together, add a ladle of hot sauce, then return to the pan off the heat and warm through without boiling. Sharpen with lemon.
Fold in the veal, onions and mushrooms, scatter with parsley and serve with rice.

name: Poulet Basquaise
blurb: Chicken braised with peppers, tomatoes, onions and a little chorizo, Basque-style, over rice.
ingredients: 1 tsp piment d'Espelette or mild chilli
method: Brown the chicken all over in a wide pan, then set aside. Fry the chorizo for 2 minutes and lift out too.
Cook the onions and peppers in the coloured fat for 12 minutes until soft and sweet. Add the garlic and piment d'Espelette for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, then add the tomatoes, bay and thyme.
Return the chicken and chorizo, cover and simmer for 25 minutes, then uncover for 10 more to thicken.
Check the seasoning and serve over rice.

name: Beef Daube Provençal
blurb: Beef slow-braised in red wine with orange peel, olives and herbs until it collapses.
ingredients: 1.2kg beef shin or chuck, in large chunks
2 bay leaves, sprig of rosemary and thyme
Mashed or boiled potatoes, to serve
method: The night before, marinate the beef in the wine with the onions, carrots, garlic, orange peel and herbs.
Next day, strain, keeping the wine and vegetables separate. Pat the beef dry and brown it hard in a casserole, then set aside.
Fry the lardons and the marinated vegetables until coloured, stir in the tomato purée, then pour in the wine and let it bubble for 5 minutes.
Return the beef with the orange peel and herbs, top up with water to almost cover, cover and cook at 150C for 3 hours until fork-tender.
Stir in the olives, rest for 20 minutes, skim the fat, and serve with potatoes to mop the sauce.

name: Pollo al Ajillo (Spanish Garlic Chicken)
blurb: Chicken pieces fried golden with a whole head of garlic, sherry and bay — a tapas bar classic scaled up.
ingredients: 1 chicken, jointed into small pieces (or 8 thighs, halved)
1 whole head of garlic, cloves peeled and lightly crushed
Fried or crushed potatoes and crusty bread, to serve
method: Season the chicken generously. Heat the oil in a wide pan and fry the chicken in a single layer, turning, for 12-15 minutes until deep golden and nearly cooked.
Add the garlic cloves and bay and fry gently for 3-4 minutes until the garlic is soft and nutty, not burnt.
Stir in the paprika and chilli flakes, then pour in the sherry and let it bubble and reduce to a glossy pan juice.
Cover and cook 5 minutes more until the chicken is cooked through.
Shower with parsley and serve with potatoes and bread for the garlicky oil.

name: Fabada Asturiana
blurb: A rich Asturian bean stew with chorizo, morcilla and smoked pork, barely spiced, deeply savoury.
ingredients: 500g dried large white beans (fabes or butter beans), soaked overnight
200g smoked pork belly or gammon, in one piece
method: Drain the beans and put them in a wide pot with the chorizo, morcilla, pork belly, onion, garlic and bay. Cover with cold water by 4cm.
Bring slowly to a simmer, skimming off any foam. Add the paprika and saffron.
Cook very gently, barely bubbling, for about 1 hour 15, adding a splash of cold water now and then to 'scare' the beans and keep them whole, until they are creamy and tender.
Lift out the meats, slice them, and return to the pot. Discard the onion and bay.
Let it settle off the heat for 15 minutes so the broth thickens, then serve in deep bowls with bread.

name: Bacalhau à Brás
blurb: Portuguese comfort food: flaked salt cod, straw potatoes and onions bound in soft scrambled egg.
ingredients: 500g salt cod, soaked 24-36 hours with water changes (or 500g fresh cod, lightly salted for 1 hour)
600g potatoes, cut into fine matchsticks (or 300g ready-made straw potatoes)
method: Poach the cod in barely simmering water for 8 minutes, drain, and flake into large pieces, discarding skin and bones.
Fry the potato matchsticks in batches in hot oil until crisp and golden; drain on paper. (Skip if using ready-made.)
Soften the onions and garlic in 3 tbsp olive oil over low heat for 12 minutes until sweet.
Add the flaked cod and warm through, then the crisp potatoes, tossing gently.
Pour in the beaten eggs and stir over low heat for a minute until just softly set — it should be creamy, not dry. Off the heat, fold through olives and parsley and serve at once.

name: Albóndigas en Salsa
blurb: Spanish pork-and-beef meatballs simmered in a smoky tomato and almond sauce.
ingredients: 50g breadcrumbs soaked in 4 tbsp milk (or water)
1 egg, 3 garlic cloves crushed, small bunch parsley
method: Mix both minces with the soaked breadcrumbs, egg, half the garlic, half the parsley, paprika and cumin. Roll into 24 walnut-sized balls.
Brown the meatballs all over in a little oil, then lift out.
Soften the onion in the same pan for 8 minutes, add the rest of the garlic and the extra paprika for 1 minute.
Add the wine and reduce, then the tomatoes and ground almonds, and simmer 5 minutes.
Return the meatballs, cover and simmer for 15 minutes until cooked through and the sauce is thick. Finish with parsley and serve with bread.

name: Pisto with Fried Eggs
blurb: Spain's answer to ratatouille — soft stewed peppers, courgette and tomato — topped with a runny egg.
method: Soften the onions in the oil over medium-low heat for 8 minutes.
Add the peppers and cook 10 minutes until floppy, then the courgettes and garlic for 5 minutes more.
Stir in the tomatoes, paprika and sugar, season, and simmer gently for 15 minutes until jammy and most of the liquid has gone.
Make wells in the pisto and crack in the eggs, or fry them separately. Cover and cook 3-4 minutes until the whites are set but the yolks runny.
Serve straight from the pan with plenty of bread.

name: Currywurst mit Pommes
blurb: Berlin street food: sliced bratwurst under a spiced curry-ketchup sauce, with a pile of chips.
ingredients: 1 tbsp mild curry powder, plus extra to finish
method: Get the chips cooking.
Simmer the ketchup, passata, vinegar, Worcestershire, curry powder, paprika, cayenne and sugar in a small pan for 8-10 minutes until glossy and thick. Taste and adjust the heat.
Grill or fry the sausages until browned and cooked through, then slice into 2cm pieces.
Pile the sausage onto plates, spoon over the warm sauce and dust with more curry powder.
Serve with the chips and extra sauce for dunking.

name: Käsespätzle
blurb: Soft hand-scraped egg noodles baked with mountain cheese and a heap of sticky fried onions.
method: Whisk the flour, eggs, water, salt and nutmeg into a thick, sticky batter and rest 15 minutes.
Fry the onions slowly in the butter for 20 minutes until deep golden and jammy.
Bring a large pan of salted water to the boil. Press the batter through a colander or spätzle grater into the water in batches; when the noodles float, give them 1 minute, then scoop out.
Layer the spätzle with the grated cheese in a baking dish, finishing with cheese.
Bake at 200C for 10 minutes until molten, top with the fried onions and chives, and serve with a sharp salad.

name: Steak & Kidney Pudding
blurb: A proper steamed suet pudding with a dark, gravy-rich filling of beef and kidney.
ingredients: 150g ox or lamb kidney, trimmed and diced
For the pastry: 300g self-raising flour, 150g shredded suet, pinch of salt, about 180ml cold water
method: Toss the steak and kidney in seasoned flour. Brown in batches, then add the onion for 5 minutes. Add the stock and Worcestershire, bring to a simmer, then cool completely (the filling goes in raw-ish; the steaming cooks it).
Rub the suet into the flour and salt, add enough water to make a soft dough. Roll out three-quarters and line a buttered 1.2-litre pudding basin.
Spoon in the filling and its gravy. Roll the rest of the dough into a lid, dampen the edges and seal.
Cover with pleated baking paper and foil, tie with string, and steam in a covered pan of simmering water (halfway up the basin) for 3 hours 30, topping up the water as needed.
Turn out, or serve from the basin wrapped in a napkin, with mash and greens.

name: Cornish Pasty
blurb: Shortcrust filled with beef skirt, potato, swede and onion, crimped and baked golden.
ingredients: For the pastry: 500g strong white flour, 120g cold butter, 120g lard, 1 tsp salt, about 175ml cold water
350g beef skirt or chuck, cut into 1cm dice
Plenty of salt and white pepper
method: Rub the fats into the flour and salt until crumbly, add the water and bring together to a firm dough. Wrap and chill for 30 minutes.
Mix the beef, potato, swede and onion and season very generously — this is the key.
Divide the pastry into 4 and roll each into a 20cm circle. Pile a quarter of the filling on one half, add a knob of butter, and leave a border.
Brush the edge with egg, fold over and crimp the seam into a rope along the top. Cut a small steam hole.
Glaze with egg and bake at 200C for 15 minutes, then 165C for 45 minutes until deep golden. Cool for 15 minutes before eating.

name: Bubble & Squeak with a Fried Egg
blurb: Leftover potato and greens fried into a crisp, craggy cake and topped with a runny egg.
ingredients: 500g cooked potato (leftover mash or boiled and crushed)
250g cooked greens — cabbage, sprouts, kale or leftover roast veg — chopped
Brown sauce or ketchup, to serve
method: Fry the onion in half the butter until soft. Mix into the potato and greens and season well.
Heat the rest of the butter and the oil in a non-stick frying pan. Press the mixture in to a thick cake and cook, undisturbed, for 6-7 minutes until a deep crust forms underneath.
Break it up roughly with a spatula, turn the pieces, press down again and cook another 5-6 minutes so plenty of edges catch and crisp.
Fry the eggs to your liking in a second pan.
Serve the bubble and squeak topped with the eggs and a squeeze of brown sauce.

name: Cheese & Onion Pie
blurb: A double-crust pie of sweet softened onions and mature cheddar, a proper Northern tea.
ingredients: Baked beans or peas, to serve
method: Cook the onions in the butter over low heat for 20-25 minutes until very soft and pale gold. Cool completely.
Mix the cooled onions with the cheese, crème fraîche, mustard, thyme and plenty of black pepper.
Line a 22cm pie dish with two-thirds of the pastry. Add the filling and level it.
Roll the rest for a lid, seal and crimp the edges, cut a couple of vents, and glaze with egg.
Bake at 200C for 30-35 minutes until deep golden. Rest 10 minutes and serve with beans or peas.
